subject: redPanda
pitch:
Category: Animal.
Subject: red panda balancing on a mossy stone.
Style: Genshin Impact.
reasoning:
I'm planning the red panda's design with a cream face mask, big rimmed ears, rust-colored body, dark belly, and fluffy ringed tail perched on a mossy stone, aiming for a Genshin-style cel-shaded look with bold toon outlines and anime eyes.

Working out the skeleton now: hip joint positioned on top of the stone, a spine chain curving upward through the torso using a catmull path, then a neck and head joint for attaching the face.

Positioning ears on the head surface using local offset coordinates relative to the head bone, working through the left/right convention so ears mirror correctly across the model's x-axis.

Adding more inset layers...

For the face, I'm placing a flattened cream sphere mask on the front of the head using a scaled sphere geometry, then working out eye placement as decals on the head surface with directional offsets and mirroring for symmetry.

Now I'm figuring out the geometry so the eyes sit correctly on the sphere's curved surface—calculating the forward offset based on the sphere radius and lateral position so the decal lands right at the surface rather than floating or sinking in. I'm adding a small nose sphere near the center-front of the head, then moving on to building the body as a swept shape following a spine path through the hip and spine joints.

For the body I'm considering a chunky radius function that varies along the sweep length, then applying toon-style cel shading with rust and cream tones for the belly countershading to get that stylized look. For the legs, I'm thinking through how the panda should be posed sitting on a stone surface, deciding between a balancing stance with limbs reaching down to specific foot targets versus a simpler chain-based approach for the leg joints.

Now I'm planning the arms as chain structures sprouting from the spine's shoulder joint, defining curved paths outward and downward with named joint segments for shoulder and elbow bends. For the tail, I'm designing a fluffy curled chain going back and up from the hips with a tapering radius, and considering color bands along its length to create a ringed, striped appearance.

For the ground stone, I'm sketching a lathe-generated flattened boulder shape with mossy top patches painted based on surface normal direction, deciding how to anchor it near the root since it isn't attached to a specific joint.

Checking the tail position—it hangs from hips down to y 0.28, which should clear the stone top at 0.31 except near center; since the tail sits at z -0.3, it's likely beyond the stone's radius anyway so no clipping issue.

For the hind legs, I'm sketching a curved path from hip to stone-top foot position using a simple sweep with tube radius 0.055 and a sphere for the foot, without needing a separate knee joint.

I'll keep the rig simple with named parent-child chains for the legs, give the balancing pose a raised side arm, tilt the head slightly, and add small ears near the top. Now I'm defining the color palette: rust, cream, dark brown, and a mottled stone gray, aiming to keep the whole script around 250 lines.

Working out the ear geometry and attachment point relative to the head's local coordinate system.

Still positioning facial features...

I figure the ink eyes should work fine placed over the cream mask area. For left/right placement, mirroring with s>0 flips to the creature's left eye correctly, matching the default right-eye drawing convention. For the head sphere part, I'm positioning it at the head joint's own anchor point so the geometry aligns naturally with the bone.

I'll define a HEAD constant for the joint position and apply a slight non-uniform scale to the sphere for a less perfectly round shape. For the body, I'm sweeping a loft along a catmull-rom path with a radius function that varies slightly to suggest a belly curve, bound to the hips and spine bone chain, making sure the body's top radius clears the head joint without overlap.

For the legs I'm working out a path from hip to knee to ankle, adjusting coordinates so the foot lands properly on the stone's surface rather than floating past its edge, then naming three joints (hip, knee, ankle) so the chain gets a proper tip joint I can attach a small flattened sphere foot to.

For the arms, I'm setting up a similar shoulder-elbow-wrist chain branching off the spine, reaching forward and out to the side for balance, with dark brown paw spheres attached at the wrist tips, scaled flatter to look paw-like.

For the tail, I'm defining a hips-anchored chain curving outward and upward through three tail joints with a tapering sweep radius, then banding it with alternating rust and dark rings finishing in a cream tip.

For the stone, I'm lathing a simple outline anchored to the hips joint and painting it with a height-based blend: mossy green noise above a threshold, rocky gray-brown noise below.

Tail sitting above the floor at that z-position checks out, and the tail shape being sphere-ish with hips resting on the stone top works fine. Now I'm thinking about the eye decal placement targeting the head surface.

I need to reference the head part variable for that. I'm also considering small moss clumps as flattened spheres scattered on the stone top, checking their positions sink slightly into the surface which is fine. Starting to write the actual code now with imports.

Setting up the builder with createBuilder, catmull, paint, mix, noise, and the toon kit utilities, then building out the panda's joint hierarchy starting with hips and a spine chain using a catmull curve.

Still writing joint hierarchy...

Now I'm working out the ear geometry, using extruded outlines positioned relative to the head bone with mirroring for left/right sides, then planning a smaller inner-ear outline on top.

Placing the eye decal on the head using forward/up offsets with mirroring for the opposite side, then adding a small ink-colored nose sphere scaled flatter and wider near the front of the face, and considering whether to include a mouth at all.

I'm deciding to skip the mouth and cheek ruffs since the mask already covers that area, and thinking about whether eyebrows are needed given the anime eye component likely includes them. For the stylized outline look, I'm weighing using ink lines along mask edges rather than true cel-shaded outlines, and sketching out a body sweep that oscillates in width along the spine using a sine-based profile, bound to the hips and spine chain together.

Now I'm working out how to layer a cream belly patch over the rust body using angular sectors, deciding to use plain color strings rather than paint objects for sector fills to keep things simple while the base body still uses cel-shaded paints. I'm planning legs as rust-colored sweeps along the leg chain with dark brown paw spheres, tail bands as colored segments, and setting up some hex color constants before starting on the eye decal with an iris color.

Then I'm adding amber eyes, importing paint/mix/noise helpers for a stone texture, placing mossy clumps near the hips with a green color, and double-checking that the hips bone anchors these extra parts correctly. Finally I'm reviewing how the chain and joint naming works before writing out the complete code.
